mainTopic: The ראש השנה and fast-day שופר in the מקדש: its plating, hearing it alongside trumpets, the יובל blessings, and the start of the משנה on a damaged שופר
overview: The גמרא works through the משנה's description of the שופר blown in the מקדש on ראש השנה. It first explains that the gold plating at the שופר's mouth was near the lips, not where the lips touch, so the שופר stayed כשר. Next it asks how the שופר could be heard over the two trumpets blown beside it. At first it says the end of the long שופר blast was heard alone. A משנה about blowing into a pit knocks down that idea, so the גמרא answers that two sounds from two different sources can be heard, especially when the sound is dear to the listeners, as with הלל and מגילה. The long שופר blast is then explained as a sign that the שופר is the main מצוה of the day. The גמרא explains why the fast-day שופר uses silver and the ראש השנה שופר uses gold. It then rules that blowing שופר together with trumpets was done only in the מקדש. Last, it discusses the line 'זה היום תחלת מעשיך' and how the יובל can share ראש השנה's blessings, and a new משנה begins about a cracked or glued שופר.

steps.title: The mouth of the שופר was plated with gold
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה: the mouth of the ראש השנה שופר in the מקדש was plated with gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: and its mouth was plated with gold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה so that it can discuss it. This is a setup line. The challenge comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes the fancy שופר of the מקדש. Its mouth, meaning the narrow end you blow into, was covered with gold. The גמרא will now ask whether that fits with another source.

keyTerms.meaning: Its mouth, meaning the narrow end of the שופר

phrases.english: And its mouth was plated with gold.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה about the שופר used in the מקדש on ראש השנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion by quoting the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The mouth of the מקדש שופר on ראש השנה was gold-plated.

steps.title: A ברייתא says gold where the lips go makes the שופר unfit
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a שופר plated with gold where the mouth is placed is פסול, which seems to contradict the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: if one plated the שופר with gold at the place where the mouth is put, it is פסול. If it is not at the place where the mouth is put, it is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה with a ברייתא that says gold at the mouth makes the שופר unfit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If gold covers the spot where the lips touch, the person is blowing through gold and not through the שופר itself, so it is פסול. The משנה, however, says the מקדש שופר had a gold-plated mouth. How could the מקדש use a שופר that is פסול?

keyTerms.meaning: But was it not taught in a ברייתא? This phrase introduces a contradicting source.
The place where one puts his mouth

phrases.english: But was it not taught: if he plated it with gold
phrases.notes: Introduces a ברייתא that seems to clash with the משנה.

phrases.english: at the place where the mouth is put, it is unfit;
not at the place where the mouth is put, it is fit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the משנה quoted in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that the mouth of the שופר was gold-plated
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says gold plating where the lips go makes a שופר פסול, so the מקדש could not have used such a שופר.

steps.title: אביי: the משנה means near the mouth, not where the lips touch
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the משנה also meant gold plating that is not where the lips are placed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: when we learned the משנה as well, we learned it as referring to a spot that is not where the mouth is placed.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the contradiction. The משנה's gold was near the mouthpiece, not on the exact spot where the lips touch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה and the ברייתא do not argue. The word 'mouth' in the משנה means the general mouth area of the שופר. The gold stopped just short of the spot where the lips go, so the ברייתא would also call it כשר.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
when we learned our Mishnah too,
we learned it as not at the place where the mouth is put.
phrases.notes: The gold was near the mouthpiece, just not on the lip spot.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר אַבָּיֵי: כִּי תְּנַן נָמֵי מַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה meant gold directly on the lip area, which would clash with the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's gold was near the mouthpiece and not where the lips touch, so it is כשר according to the ברייתא too.
steps.whatToRemember: Gold plating on the exact spot where the lips touch makes a שופר פסול. Plating elsewhere, even near the mouth, is fine. That is what the מקדש שופר had.

steps.title: Two trumpets were blown at the sides
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: two חצוצרות were blown on either side of the שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: and two חצוצרות were blown from the sides.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line from the משנה to set up a new question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מקדש on ראש השנה, the שופר was blown in the middle and a חצוצרה was blown on each side of it. The question will be whether the שופר could be heard over the trumpets.

phrases.english: And two trumpets at the sides.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two חצוצרות were blown alongside the שופר in the מקדש on ראש השנה.

steps.title: Can two sounds be heard at the same time?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the שופר could be heard with the trumpets, since a person cannot take in two sounds at once, as shown by זכור and שמור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can two sounds really be heard at once? But a ברייתא teaches: 'זכור' and 'שמור' were said in one utterance, which the mouth cannot say and the ear cannot hear!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה. If the שופר and the trumpets sound together, it seems no one could clearly hear the שופר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from the עשרת הדברות. 'זכור' and 'שמור' were said by הקב״ה at the same moment, and the ברייתא calls this something a human ear cannot hear. That shows people cannot take in two sounds at once. So the trumpets should drown out the שופר, and no one would fulfill the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Remember' and 'Keep', the two versions of the שבת commandment

steps.confusionAlert: The זכור and שמור source is not about שבת here. It is brought only to prove that a human ear cannot take in two sounds at the same time.

phrases.english: But can two sounds be heard?
But was it not taught: 'Remember' and 'Keep'
were said in one utterance,
something the mouth cannot say
and the ear cannot hear!
phrases.notes: So humans cannot take in two sounds at once.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the arrangement described in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's arrangement of trumpets sounding together with the שופר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two simultaneous sounds cannot both be heard, so the trumpets would block the שופר and the מצוה would not be fulfilled.

steps.title: That is why the שופר blew longer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the שופר blast was held longer than the trumpets, so its ending was heard alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: For this reason, the שופר is held longer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by pointing to another detail in the משנה: the שופר blast went on longer than the trumpets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the שופר is drawn out while the trumpets are short. Once the trumpets stopped, the last part of the שופר blast was heard clearly by itself. That last part is what let people fulfill the מצוה.

phrases.english: For this reason he draws out the shofar.
phrases.notes: This refers to the משנה's line that the שופר is long and the trumpets are short.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to another detail in the משנה that solves the problem
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The trumpets would block the entire שופר blast.
steps.terutzMaskana: The end of the שופר blast is heard alone after the trumpets stop.

steps.title: Does hearing only part of a תקיעה count?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether this means that hearing only the end of a תקיעה counts, and so also only the beginning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that if one heard the end of a תקיעה without its beginning, he is יוצא? And it would follow that hearing the beginning without the end also makes him יוצא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the last answer and asks whether it is true. This sets up the next move, a test from a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מקדש, people only heard the end of the שופר blast clearly. So it seems hearing part of a תקיעה is enough. If the end alone is enough, then logically the beginning alone should be enough too.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say? It introduces an implication being tested.

phrases.english: Is this to say that when one hears the end of a blast
without the beginning of the blast, he has fulfilled his obligation,
and it follows: the beginning of a blast
without the end of the blast, he has fulfilled his obligation?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a broader rule out of the answer in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether hearing only part of a תקיעה, either the end or the beginning, is enough to be יוצא.

steps.title: Then why does one long blast count as only one?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: a very long final תקיעה counts as only one. If part of a blast counts, it should count as two.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if he blew the first תקיעה, and drew out the second one as long as two, he has only one in hand. Why? Let it count for him as two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the idea from step 7 against a משנה that seems to contradict it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A set of blasts is תקיעה, תרועה, תקיעה. Suppose someone stretches the last תקיעה of a set to double length. If half a blast counts, the first half should close this set and the second half should open the next set. Yet the משנה says it counts as only one, so it seems that part of a blast does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear. It introduces a source used as proof or challenge.
He has only one to his credit
Let it count for him as two

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If he blew the first (tekiah)
phrases.notes: The opening תקיעה of the first set.

phrases.english: and drew out the second (tekiah) as long as two,
phrases.notes: The closing תקיעה of the set was stretched to double length.

phrases.english: he has only one in hand.
Why? Let it count for him as two!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses a משנה to challenge the idea raised in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that part of a תקיעה is enough
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If half a blast counts, a double-length blast should count as two blasts. The משנה says it counts as only one.

steps.title: We do not split one blast into two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that part of a blast does count, but one continuous blast cannot be divided into two separate תקיעות.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not cut blasts apart from each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The long blast counts as only one because one continuous blast cannot be split into two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה about the long blast does not show that a partial blast fails. It teaches a different rule: one unbroken sound counts as one blast and cannot be divided between two sets. So the idea from the מקדש stands: hearing part of a תקיעה is enough.
steps.whatToRemember: One continuous blast always counts as a single תקיעה and cannot be split to count for two. The idea that hearing only part of a תקיעה is enough is challenged in the next step, and in step 11 the גמרא drops it.

phrases.english: Dividing blasts from one another, we do not divide.
phrases.notes: One continuous blast is one תקיעה, even though a part of a blast would be valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8 and leaves the idea of step 7 standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Separates the משנה's rule from the question of partial blasts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The long blast counts as one because a partial blast is not valid.
steps.terutzMaskana: A partial blast is valid, but one continuous blast is never divided into two תקיעות.

steps.title: Blowing into a pit shows that part of a blast does not count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: someone who blows שופר into a pit and hears an echo has not fulfilled the מצוה. If part of a blast counted, he should be יוצא with the clear beginning, before the echo mixed in.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if someone blows into a pit, a cistern, or a large jug, and he heard the sound of the שופר, he has fulfilled his obligation. If he heard an echo, he has not. Why not? He should be יוצא with the beginning of the blast, before the sound got mixed up with the echo!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה that seems to prove that hearing only part of a תקיעה does not count. This goes against what was said in steps 6 and 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the very start of the blast, only the clear שופר sound is heard. The echo comes a moment later. If hearing part of a blast were enough, the start alone should count. Since the משנה says he is not יוצא, part of a blast must not be enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source as a proof or a challenge
A pit / a cistern / a large jug: hollow places that make an echo
An echo, an unclear blurred sound
Before the sound gets mixed up

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the echo spoils the whole blast from the start. The point is that the beginning WAS clear, and still it does not count. That is exactly why it shows that part of a blast is not enough.

phrases.english: Come and hear: one who blows into a pit
or into a cistern
or into a large jug,
if he heard the sound of the shofar, he has fulfilled his obligation,
phrases.notes: The clear sound of the שופר

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם קוֹל הֲבָרָה שְׁמַע — לֹא יָצָא.
phrases.english: but if he heard the sound of an echo, he has not fulfilled his obligation.
Why? Let him fulfill it with the beginning of the blast,
phrases.notes: Based on the idea that part of a blast counts

phrases.english: before the sound becomes mixed up!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 9's claim, which also stood behind step 6, that hearing part of a תקיעה counts.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that hearing only part of a blast is enough (steps 6 and 9).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The beginning of a blast into a pit is heard clearly, before any echo. If part of a blast counted, the listener would be יוצא. The משנה says he is not, so part of a blast does not count.

steps.title: Two sounds from one source cannot be heard, but from two sources they can
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops its earlier answer and gives a new one. Two sounds coming from one source cannot both be taken in. Two sounds from two different sources can, so the שופר and the trumpets could both be heard.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: two sounds from one person cannot be heard. Two sounds from two people can be heard.
steps.whatsHappening: The word אלא shows that the גמרא is giving up the answer from step 6. It gives a new answer to the question from step 5 about hearing the שופר together with the trumpets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof from זכור and שמור was about two words coming from ONE speaker at the same moment. That is impossible for a person to take in, which is why it was a miracle. The שופר and the trumpets came from two different blowers, so they can be heard together. Now there is no need to say the שופר lasted longer.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: the earlier answer is dropped and a new one is given

steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not respond to the pit challenge. It accepts that challenge and goes back to answer the original question from step 5 in a new way.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up a clear rule for the rest of the סוגיא: whether two sounds can be heard depends on whether they come from one source or from two.

phrases.english: Rather: two sounds from one person
cannot be heard,
from two people, they can be heard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 10, drops the answer of step 6, and answers step 5 in a new way.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retraction and new distinction: one source versus two sources
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שופר was heard only because its ending lasted longer than the trumpets, and that end alone counted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The זכור/שמור rule applies only to one speaker. Sounds from two separate blowers can both be heard.

steps.title: A ברייתא says two people may not read the תורה at once
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new answer. A ברייתא says that at the תורה reading only one reads and one translates, not two reading and two translating. This suggests that even two people's voices cannot be heard together.
steps.simpleTranslation: But can two sounds from two people really be heard? It was taught in a ברייתא: for the תורה reading, one reads and one translates, as long as there are not two reading and two translating!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new rule from step 11 with a ברייתא about the public reading of the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two readers are two different people. If two people's voices could be heard together, two people could read at once. The ברייתא forbids this, which suggests that listeners cannot follow two people at the same time.

keyTerms.meaning: Can they really be heard? (a challenging question)
But it was taught in a ברייתא
Translates aloud into Aramaic for the listeners
As long as, on condition that

phrases.english: But from two people, can they be heard?
But it was taught in a baraita:
In the Torah reading, one reads and one translates,
as long as there are not
two reading and two translating!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִתְּרֵי גַבְרֵי מִי מִשְׁתַּמְעִי? וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule from step 11 that sounds from two people can be heard.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 11 that two sounds from two people can be heard.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two readers are two separate people, yet the ברייתא forbids two from reading at once. So two people's voices apparently cannot be heard together.

steps.title: Something dear gets full attention, so both sounds are heard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the שופר is like the second half of that same ברייתא. Even ten people may read הלל and מגילה together, because these are dear to people and they listen closely. The שופר is also dear, so people listen closely and hear it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This case is only like the second half of the ברייתא: with הלל and מגילה, even ten people may read together. We see that since it is dear, a person pays attention. Here too, since it is dear, he pays attention and hears.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 12. It uses the second half of the same ברייתא to show that the שופר is a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally two people's voices are hard to follow, which is why the תורה reading allows only one reader. When something is precious to people, as with הלל, מגילה, and שופר, they concentrate hard and can take in the sound even with another sound going on. So the שופר could be heard over the trumpets.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only like the second half (of the ברייתא)

steps.whatToRemember: Two sounds from one source can never both be taken in, which is why זכור and שמור was a miracle. Two sounds from two sources are normally hard to follow. When the matter is dear to people, they concentrate and can hear it, as with הלל, מגילה, and שופר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how the שופר could be heard while the trumpets were also blowing. It also teaches that how much a person cares about something can affect what he is able to hear.

phrases.english: This is only similar to the latter clause:
with Hallel and the Megillah,
even ten may read.
Apparently, since it is dear, one pays attention,
here too, since it is dear,
one pays attention and hears.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12 and defends the rule from step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: things that are dear get special attention
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling about the תורה reading shows that two people's voices can never be heard together.
steps.terutzMaskana: When a matter is dear, like הלל, מגילה, or שופר, listeners concentrate and can hear one sound even while another sound is going on.

steps.title: Then why is the שופר blown longer?
steps.stepSummary: If both sounds can be heard together, why does the משנה make the שופר blast longer than the trumpets?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then why does he blow a long blast with the שופר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge based on the answer it just gave. If people can hear the שופר even while the trumpets are blowing, why make the שופר blast last longer?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that on ראש השנה the שופר blows long and the trumpets blow short. The earlier thought was that the long blast lets the שופר be heard alone at the end. But step 13 said people hear the שופר anyway because it is dear to them, so the extra length now seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes long; blows a long blast
But then; if so (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But then why does he blow a long blast with the shofar?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges a detail of the משנה in light of the answer given in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that the שופר blows long on ראש השנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the שופר is heard even together with the trumpets, there is no reason to make it longer so that it can be heard alone.

steps.title: To show the מצוה of the day is the שופר
steps.stepSummary: The longer שופר blast shows everyone that the main מצוה of the day is the שופר, not the trumpets.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that people know that the מצוה of the day is with the שופר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the long blast is not needed for hearing. It is there to make clear that the שופר is the main מצוה of ראש השנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for the long blast changes. It is not about whether people can hear the שופר. It is a public signal that the שופר, not the trumpets, is what the day is about.

keyTerms.meaning: The מצוה of the day; the day's main obligation

steps.whatToRemember: The שופר blows longer on ראש השנה to show that it is the main מצוה of the day, not because otherwise it could not be heard.

phrases.english: To make known that the מצוה of the day is with the shofar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a new reason for the rule (showing importance, not making it audible).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The long blast seemed to exist only so the שופר could be heard alone.
steps.terutzMaskana: The long blast shows that the שופר is the main מצוה of the day.

steps.title: The משנה on the fast-day shofar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: on fast days the שופר is made from curved rams' horns with a silver-plated mouthpiece.
steps.simpleTranslation: And on fast days, the שופר is from curved rams' horns, and its mouth is plated with silver.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה to discuss it. It is setting up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the משנה said the ראש השנה שופר was plated with gold. Now it says the fast-day שופר is plated with silver. This difference is what the גמרא will ask about.

phrases.english: And on fast days, with curved rams' horns
and its mouth is plated with silver.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new section of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On fast days, a curved ram's horn with a silver-plated mouthpiece is used.

steps.title: Why gold there and silver here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ראש השנה שופר is plated with gold while the fast-day שופר is plated with silver.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different there, that it is gold, and what is different here, that it is silver?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question: why does the משנה use a different metal for each day?
steps.deeperAnalysis: "There" means ראש השנה (gold) and "here" means fast days (silver). The גמרא wants a reason for the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? (asks for the reason behind a distinction)

phrases.english: What is different there, that it is gold,
and what is different here, that it is silver?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the משנה line just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for gold on ראש השנה and silver on fast days.

steps.title: Gathering instruments are made of silver
steps.stepSummary: First answer: anything used to gather the people is made of silver, as the פסוק about the silver trumpets shows.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: every gathering is with silver, as it is written: "Make for yourself two silver trumpets."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer. Fast days are gatherings of the people, and the תורה uses silver for gathering the people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a fast day the community gathers to pray. The פסוק commands silver trumpets for calling the people together, so silver fits instruments used to gather people.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (introduces one possible answer)
A gathering or assembly of people

phrases.english: If you want, say:
every gathering is done with silver,
as it is written: "Make for yourself two trumpets of silver."
phrases.notes: במדבר י:ב; those trumpets were used to call the congregation together.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא כָּל כִּינּוּפְיָא דְּכֶסֶף הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Fast days are gatherings, and the תורה uses silver for gathering the people.

steps.title: The תורה saves Jewish money
steps.stepSummary: Second answer: the תורה cares about the money of the Jewish people, so it uses cheaper silver.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: the תורה has pity on the money of the Jewish people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer. Silver is used because it costs less than gold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer is not about gathering at all. It says the תורה avoids putting unnecessary expense on people, so it uses the cheaper metal. This sets up the next challenge.

keyTerms.term: הַתּוֹרָה חָסָה עַל מָמוֹנָן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
keyTerms.meaning: The תורה has pity on (protects) the money of the Jewish people

phrases.english: And if you want, say:

phrases.aramaic: הַתּוֹרָה חָסָה עַל מָמוֹנָן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: The Torah has pity on the money of the Jewish people.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא הַתּוֹרָה חָסָה עַל מָמוֹנָן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, independent answer to the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Silver is used to save the people money.

steps.title: Then use silver on ראש השנה too
steps.stepSummary: If the תורה wants to save money, the ראש השנה שופר should also be plated with silver.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, let us make it with silver!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second answer. If saving money is the reason, it should apply on ראש השנה as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saving money would be a reason on every day, so it cannot explain why ראש השנה uses gold. The challenge targets only the second answer, since the first (gathering) does not apply to ראש השנה.

phrases.english: There too, let us make it of silver!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason that the תורה saves Jewish money.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Saving money applies equally on ראש השנה, so the gold there needs an explanation.

steps.title: Honoring the יום טוב comes first
steps.stepSummary: Even so, honoring the יום טוב outweighs saving money, so ראש השנה gets gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, the honor of the יום טוב comes first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that on ראש השנה the honor of the holiday is more important than saving money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saving money is a real concern, but כבוד יום טוב outweighs it. A fast day is not a יום טוב, so there is nothing to outweigh the money concern, and silver is used.
steps.whatToRemember: Fast day: silver (gathering, or saving money). ראש השנה: gold, because כבוד יום טוב outweighs the cost.

phrases.english: Even so,
the honor of the festival takes priority.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ הָכִי כְּבוֹד יוֹם טוֹב עֲדִיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Weighing values: a stronger reason overrides the money concern on ראש השנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Saving money should apply on ראש השנה too.
steps.terutzMaskana: On ראש השנה, כבוד יום טוב outweighs saving money.

steps.title: רב פפא בר שמואל wanted to follow the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא בר שמואל planned to actually practice the משנה's arrangement of שופר together with trumpets.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא בר שמואל thought to act in practice according to our משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story to set up a practical ruling. רב פפא בר שמואל wanted to blow שופר and trumpets together, as the משנה describes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question now becomes practical: does the משנה's arrangement apply everywhere? The next step answers it.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who wanted to follow the משנה in practice

phrases.english: Rav Pappa bar Shmuel
thought to act in practice according to our Mishnah.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל סָבַר לְמִיעְבַּד עוֹבָדָא כְּמַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining the משנה to whether it applies in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב פפא בר שמואל held that the משנה's arrangement should be practiced.

steps.title: רבא: only in the Temple
steps.stepSummary: רבא told him that the משנה's arrangement was said only for the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: they said this only in the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects רב פפא בר שמואל's plan. Blowing שופר together with trumpets applies only in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's rules are correct, but they describe what was done in the מקדש. They do not tell us what to do in other places.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not rejecting the משנה. He is limiting where it applies: only in the מקדש.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
They said this only in the Temple.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לָא אָמְרוּ אֶלָּא בְּמִקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the plan of step 22.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects applying the משנה's arrangement outside the מקדש.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב פפא בר שמואל assumed the משנה applied everywhere, but it describes the מקדש only.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא confirms that outside the מקדש, a place with trumpets has no שופר, and a place with שופר has no trumpets.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: when is this said? In the מקדש. But outside it, where there are trumpets there is no שופר, and where there is a שופר there are no trumpets.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רבא. Outside the מקדש, the שופר and trumpets are never used together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא limits the משנה's case to the מקדש, just as רבא said. Outside the מקדש (בגבולין), fast days use trumpets without a שופר, and ראש השנה uses a שופר without trumpets.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא supports the statement)
In what case are these words said?
The outlying areas, anywhere outside the מקדש

steps.whatToRemember: שופר together with trumpets is done only in the מקדש. Everywhere else it is one or the other: trumpets on fast days, שופר on ראש השנה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical הלכה: today, without the מקדש, we blow only the שופר on ראש השנה, with no trumpets.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
In what case are these words said? In the Temple,
but in the outlying areas,
a place where there are trumpets has no shofar,
and a place where there is a shofar has no trumpets.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's ruling in step 23.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that the משנה applies only in the מקדש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that outside the מקדש the שופר and trumpets are never used together.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Outside the מקדש, a place with trumpets has no שופר, and a place with שופר has no trumpets.

steps.title: Great rabbis tried the practice, but the חכמים limited it to the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: רבי חלפתא and רבי חנניא בן תרדיון set up this practice in their towns, but the חכמים ruled it was done only at the Temple.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חלפתא set up this practice in ציפורי, and so did רבי חנניא בן תרדיון in סיכני. When the matter reached the חכמים, they said: this was done only at the eastern gates and on the הר הבית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the same ברייתא from the last step. It shows that even great rabbis who used שופר with trumpets outside the מקדש were corrected by the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the strongest part of the proof for רבא's ruling to רב פפא בר שמואל. Even רבי חלפתא and רבי חנניא בן תרדיון did what רב פפא בר שמואל wanted to do, and the חכמים said it belongs only to the Temple area.

keyTerms.meaning: Set up a practice; established a custom
ציפורי, a town in the גליל
סיכני, a town in the גליל
The eastern gates of the Temple

steps.whyThisMatters: It confirms in practice that we do not blow trumpets together with the שופר today.

phrases.english: And so Rabbi Chalafta established this practice in Tzippori
and Rabbi Chananya ben Teradyon did so in Sikhni
and when the matter came before the Sages, they said:
They did not act this way
phrases.notes: They did not blow שופר together with trumpets.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בְּשַׁעֲרֵי מִזְרָח וּבְהַר הַבַּיִת בִּלְבַד.
phrases.english: except at the eastern gates and on the Temple Mount alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא begun in step 24, adding a precedent and the ruling of the חכמים.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's statement that the משנה's arrangement of שופר with trumpets applied only in the מקדש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling of the חכמים in the ברייתא against the practice of רבי חלפתא and רבי חנניא בן תרדיון.

steps.title: The verse showing trumpets plus שופר is only 'before the King'
steps.stepSummary: רבא (or רבי יהושע בן לוי) brings a verse in תהלים showing that trumpets and שופר together are needed only before 'the King, ה׳', meaning in the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said, and some say רבי יהושע בן לוי said: What is the verse? It is written: 'With trumpets and the sound of a שופר, make noise before the King, ה׳.' Only before the King, ה׳, do we need trumpets and the sound of a שופר, but in general, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the verse behind the rule that שופר together with trumpets is only for the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'before the King, ה׳' are read as pointing to the בית המקדש, where the שכינה is present. So the pairing of trumpets with שופר is tied to that place, and outside it we do not use both.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (another version of who said it)
What is the verse (that this comes from)?
Before the King, ה׳ (understood as the מקדש)

steps.whatToRemember: Blowing שופר together with trumpets was a מקדש-only practice. The source is 'לפני המלך ה׳'. Outside the מקדש we blow only the שופר on ראש השנה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: Rava said, and some say it was Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:
What is the verse?
As it is written: 'With trumpets and the sound of a shofar'
make noise before the King, ה׳' (Tehillim 98:6)
It is before the King, ה׳, that we need
trumpets and the sound of a shofar
but in general, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural source for the rule the ברייתא just stated.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that trumpets with שופר are only for the מקדש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים צח:ו, 'בחצוצרות וקול שופר הריעו לפני המלך ה׳'.

steps.title: Our ראש השנה prayer follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the יובל matching ראש השנה. רב שמואל בר יצחק says our prayer 'זה היום תחלת מעשיך' follows רבי אליעזר, who holds the world was created in תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: The יובל is the same as ראש השנה for the blowing and the blessings. רב שמואל בר יצחק said: Whose view do we follow today when we pray 'This day is the beginning of Your works, a remembrance of the first day'? It follows רבי אליעזר, who said the world was created in תשרי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה about the יובל. It brings a statement about which opinion our ראש השנה prayer follows, and this sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known argument about whether the world was created in תשרי or in ניסן. Calling ראש השנה 'the beginning of Your works' only fits the view that creation happened in תשרי, which is רבי אליעזר's view.

keyTerms.meaning: The special blessings in the עמידה

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'יובל' does not mean the whole Jubilee year. It means יום כיפור of the יובל year, the day the שופר is blown to free slaves and return fields.

phrases.english: The Jubilee is the same as Rosh Hashanah
for the blowing and for the blessings, etc.
Rav Shmuel bar Yitzchak said:
According to whom do we pray nowadays
'This day is the beginning of Your works,
a remembrance of the first day'?
According to whom? According to Rabbi Eliezer
who said: The world was created in Tishrei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, moving to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ראש השנה prayer 'זה היום תחלת מעשיך' follows רבי אליעזר, who holds the world was created in תשרי.

steps.title: How can the יובל blessings match when one line does not fit?
steps.stepSummary: רב עינא objects: the משנה says the יובל and ראש השנה share the same blessings, but 'זה היום תחלת מעשיך' fits ראש השנה and not the יובל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עינא objected: The משנה says the יובל is the same as ראש השנה for the blowing and the blessings. But there is the line 'This day is the beginning of Your works, a remembrance of the first day.' It belongs on ראש השנה and does not belong on the יובל!
steps.whatsHappening: רב עינא challenges the משנה's claim that the blessings are the same. He points to the line just mentioned, which is said on ראש השנה but cannot be said on the יובל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יום כיפור of the יובל is not the day of creation, so saying 'this day is the beginning of Your works' on it would be false. That means the blessings cannot be exactly the same, which seems to contradict the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection (usually from a משנה or ברייתא)
It is not there; it does not apply

phrases.english: Rav Eina raised an objection:
The Jubilee is the same as Rosh Hashanah
for the blowing and for the blessings
But there is 'This day is the beginning of Your works,
a remembrance of the first day'
which applies on Rosh Hashanah
but does not apply on the Jubilee!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the prayer line from step 27 to challenge the משנה's statement that the blessings are the same.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's claim that the יובל and ראש השנה are the same for the blessings.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The line 'זה היום תחלת מעשיך' is only true on ראש השנה, so the blessings cannot be fully identical.

steps.title: The משנה means the rest of the blessings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה means the rest of the blessings are the same, not that every line is identical.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the משנה taught that they are the same, it was speaking about the rest of the blessings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב עינא's question. The משנה's 'same blessings' refers to the remaining parts, and the special ראש השנה line is left out on the יובל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה was not claiming word-for-word sameness. The main blessings (מלכיות, זכרונות, שופרות) are shared, while a line that only fits ראש השנה, such as 'זה היום תחלת מעשיך', is simply dropped on the יובל.

keyTerms.meaning: About the rest; the remaining parts

steps.whatToRemember: The יובל matches ראש השנה in its blowing and its main blessings. The line 'זה היום תחלת מעשיך' belongs only to ראש השנה, because it follows רבי אליעזר's view that the world was created in תשרי.

phrases.english: When it teaches this, it refers to the rest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers רב עינא's objection.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the משנה's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to mean that every word of the blessings is the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means the rest of the blessings are the same. The ראש השנה-only line is left out on the יובל.

steps.title: A second version: the יובל comparison does not follow רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי reports a different version of רב שמואל בר יצחק's statement. Here he says the משנה that makes the יובל equal to ראש השנה does not follow רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא, son of רב אידי, taught it this way: רב שמואל בר יצחק said: The משנה teaches that the יובל is the same as ראש השנה for the שופר blowing and the blessings. Whose opinion is this? It is not the opinion of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of what רב שמואל בר יצחק said. In this version he says the משנה about the יובל is NOT like רבי אליעזר. This step sets up the reason, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (step 27), רב שמואל בר יצחק linked our prayer to רבי אליעזר, and רב עינא raised the problem with the יובל. In this version, רב שמואל בר יצחק starts from the משנה about the יובל and says it does not fit רבי אליעזר. The same tension is now inside his own statement.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught it this way. This signals a different version of an earlier statement.
That which we learned (in the משנה)
The יובל is equal to ראש השנה

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. It is the same discussion as steps 27–29, told in a different version. In the first version, רב עינא raised the problem. In this version, רב שמואל בר יצחק raises it himself.

phrases.english: Rav Sheisha, son of Rav Idi,
taught it like this:
phrases.notes: Introduces an alternate version of the earlier passage

phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Yitzchak said:
That which we learned in the Mishnah,
the Jubilee is the same as Rosh Hashanah
for the shofar blowing and for the blessings,
whose opinion is it?
It is not like Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי מַתְנֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the passage in steps 27–29
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה that makes the יובל equal to ראש השנה does not follow רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: Why it cannot be רבי אליעזר: the line about the world's creation
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר holds the world was created in תשרי, so ראש השנה includes 'זה היום תחלת מעשיך'. That line cannot be said on the יובל, so the blessings would not be identical.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it were רבי אליעזר: he says the world was created in תשרי. Then there is the line 'This day is the beginning of Your works, a remembrance of the first day.' That line is said on ראש השנה but not on the יובל!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמואל בר יצחק explains why the משנה cannot follow רבי אליעזר. A line about the creation of the world belongs on ראש השנה, but it does not fit the יובל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אליעזר, ראש השנה is the anniversary of creation, so the prayer mentions it. The יובל falls on יום כיפור, which is not the anniversary of creation. So the blessings would differ, which seems to contradict the משנה's word 'שוה' (equal).

keyTerms.meaning: A remembrance of the first day (of creation)
It is there / it is not there

phrases.english: For if it were Rabbi Eliezer,
since he says
that the world was created in Tishrei,
then there is the line:
'This day is the beginning of Your works,
a remembrance of the first day,'
which is said on Rosh Hashanah,
but is not said on the Jubilee!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר בְּתִשְׁרִי נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the claim in step 30
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the משנה about the יובל does not follow רבי אליעזר
steps.raayaSupportSource: The prayer line 'זה היום תחלת מעשיך', which fits only ראש השנה under רבי אליעזר's view

steps.title: The משנה only means the rest of the blessings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the reasoning. The משנה's 'equal' refers to the rest of the blessings, so it can still follow רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the משנה said they are equal, it was talking about the rest of the blessings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב שמואל בר יצחק's reasoning. The משנה never meant every single line is the same, only the rest of the blessings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'שוה' does not demand that every word match. The one line about creation can be left out on the יובל, and the משנה can still follow רבי אליעזר. This matches the answer given in the first version (step 29).

keyTerms.meaning: When it taught (what the משנה actually meant)

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions end the same way. The משנה's comparison of the יובל and ראש השנה covers the main blessings. The creation line is said only on ראש השנה, and this fits רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: When the Mishnah taught it,
it was about the rest of the blessings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reasoning of step 31
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the conclusion that the משנה cannot follow רבי אליעזר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes 'שוה' means every line is identical, when it only means the rest of the blessings are the same

steps.title: New משנה: a cracked or pieced-together שופר is not valid
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that a שופר that cracked and was glued back together is פסול. A שופר made by gluing together broken pieces of שופרות is also פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A שופר that cracked and someone glued it back is not valid. If someone glued together broken pieces of שופרות, it is not valid.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic: which שופרות are valid for blowing. It gives two cases of repaired שופרות, and both are not valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the glued שופר looks whole, the repair makes it unfit. The second case is stronger: pieces from different broken שופרות were joined into one, so it was never one real שופר. The גמרא will explain the reasons next.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. This marks the start of a new משנה.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
A shofar that cracked and was glued together
is unfit.
If he glued together broken pieces of shofars,
it is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A cracked שופר that was glued is פסול, and a שופר assembled from glued broken pieces is פסול.
